title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Friday selloff — Dow -1.2% (-653 pts), S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.2% as oil surged on U.S.-Iran tensions; Brent crude hit $116.72/bbl (highest settle since April) and WTI jumped ~4% to $103.48. 10-yr Treasury yield rose; gold fell 1.2%.
Markets: Iran threatened wider strikes on U.S. bases, warships and civilian targets in Gulf countries if the U.S. and Israel resume attacks, keeping oil bid heading into the weekend.
Companies: American Express is cutting 5% of its workforce to speed up decision-making while raising its full-year profit outlook; shares still fell 3.7%, the worst performer on the Dow.

Companies: SK Hynix scrapped U.S. IPO plans for its flash-memory unit Solidigm citing market conditions, after a South Korean data-center IPO flopped (-30% on debut); Anthropic's IPO is still expected in November.
Macro/Policy: The Fed meets Wednesday; a heavy earnings week follows with Alphabet, Microsoft, ExxonMobil, Chevron, Coca-Cola and GE Vernova reporting.

Macro/Policy: Banks are scenario-planning for an AI 'day after' catastrophe and flagging unauthorized AI-agent activity in customer accounts (Axios); lawmakers from Sanders to DeSantis are calling for guardrails.
Macro/Policy: A 'Black October' cybersecurity scare — critical PHP vulnerabilities affecting roughly 70% of server-side websites — prompted NSA warnings and site shutdowns this week.

Macro/Policy: Diesel prices remain near record highs amid Iran-war supply disruptions; Trump unveiled $8B in farmer relief aid, while lawmakers question the legality of Russian diesel tanker imports under his deal with Moscow.
